title: Runtime serving modes: latency vs throughput standards and test methodology
author: Ava Brooks
content:
Overview:
This document defines Redwood's official runtime serving profiles ("latency-mode", "throughput-mode", and "mixed-mode"), the configuration keys that implement them, the observable SLOs we use to validate correctness, and a reproducible test methodology for regression and performance validation. It is intended for serving-runtime engineers, SREs, product owners for Dedicated/Hosted tiers, and performance-focused reviewers during model onboarding.

Scope and goals:
- Scope: applies to all model-serving clusters running the Redwood Serving Runtime (rserve) in hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Goals:
  - Provide deterministic behavior and clear expectations when a tenant selects a runtime profile.
  - Reduce variance between test-harness results and production tail-latency.
  - Standardize configuration, telemetry, and rollout steps for profile changes.

Definitions:
- latency-mode: runtime configuration optimized to minimize per-request tail latency (p95/p99) for short-to-medium requests (commonly <= 256 input tokens). Prioritizes small batches, aggressive preemption, and hot-cache residency.
- throughput-mode: runtime configuration optimized to maximize tokens-per-second (TPS) across a GPU or pod cluster for large-batch workloads. Prioritizes larger batch sizes, relaxed per-request latency, and batched KV cache handling.
- mixed-mode: a hybrid profile that uses adaptive batching and policy-based routing (fast-path for small requests, batch-path for large requests).

Profile configuration (recommended keys and example values):
| config_key | latency-mode (example) | throughput-mode (example) | mixed-mode (example) |
|-----------:|-----------------------:|--------------------------:|---------------------:|
| max_batch_size | 8 | 256 | 64 |
| batch_timeout_ms | 5 | 40 | 12 |
| preempt_small_requests | true | false | true |
| kv_cache_policy | sticky | batched-writeback | sticky-with-eviction |
| kernel_selection_preference | fp16-min-latency | int8-max-throughput | dynamic-by-input-length |
| max_concurrent_requests_per_gpu | 16 | 128 | 48 |

SLO mapping by profile (examples):
- latency-mode: p95 latency (inference-only, short requests <=128 tokens) <= 120 ms; p99 <= 300 ms; throughput >= baseline per-tenant throughput (varies by committed capacity).
- throughput-mode: tokens/sec per-GPU >= 10k (for tested large-batch workloads); p95 latency (large requests) <= 2.5x baseline baseline_lat_ms; GPU utilization > 70%.
- mixed-mode: small-request p95 <= 200 ms; aggregate TPS within 85% of throughput-mode baseline for same cluster.

Telemetry and metrics (required):
- latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms, latency_p99_ms (separate histograms for short/long requests).
- rps, tokens_per_sec, avg_batch_size, batch_timeout_ms_observed, queue_depth, preempt_events_total.
- gpu_utilization_percent, kernel_switch_count, memory_evicts_total, kv_cache_hit_ratio.
- cost_token_estimate (tokens * cost_per_token_profile) for per-request cost signals.

Testing and validation methodology (step-by-step):
1. Baseline capture:
   - Record a 24-hour production sampling of request size distribution, avg tokens, and peak concurrency. Use these to derive the synthetic workload shapes.
2. Synthetic workload definitions:
   - short-chat: 1-64 input tokens, 16 response tokens on average, Poisson arrivals at target rps.
   - mid-batch: 64-512 tokens, variable outputs, mixed arrival patterns.
   - bulk-generation: 512-4096 tokens typical for batch embed/rep generation.
3. Test harness (cli):
   - rserve-harness --target-cluster test-cluster --profile latency-mode --workload short-chat --duration 1800 --concurrency 40 --measure tail
   - rserve-harness --target-cluster test-cluster --profile throughput-mode --workload bulk-generation --duration 3600 --concurrency 256 --measure throughput
4. Acceptance criteria:
   - All target SLOs (profile-specific) met for two independent runs separated by >1 hour.
   - Observed avg_batch_size and batch_timeout_ms_observed match configured expectations within +/- 20%.
   - No increase in kernel_switch_count greater than 15% compared to baseline (preference for stable kernel paths).
5. Regression checks:
   - Run the test harness in CI against the proposed runtime change with identical seeds and workload definitions. Failure if p95 degrades by > 20% for latency-mode or tokens/sec drops > 10% for throughput-mode.

Rollout and change management:
- Canary: 5% traffic for 2 hours across geographically representative hosts. Monitor telemetry for early regressions.
- Gradual ramp: 5 -> 20 -> 50 -> 100 percent over minimum 6-hour windows, pause on any SLO breach or >10% increase in error rates.
- Automatic rollback triggers:
  - p95 degradation > 30% sustained for 10 minutes.
  - error_rate_inference > 0.5% absolute increase.
  - GPU memory OOM events.

Operational guidance and playbook (runbook steps):
1. If latency-mode p95 exceeds target:
   - Check avg_batch_size and batch_timeout_ms_observed. If avg_batch_size > configured max_batch_size, reduce batch_timeout_ms and/or max_batch_size.
   - Verify KV cache hit ratio; warm cache by replaying representative short-chat workload.
   - Inspect kernel_switch_count; if elevated, pin kernel_selection_preference to last-known-good for immediate mitigation.
2. If throughput-mode TPS drops:
   - Check queue_depth and preempt_events_total; high preemption indicates interference from latency-priority tenants. Temporarily mark throughput pods as isolated and increase max_concurrent_requests_per_gpu.
   - Check GPU clocking and power policies; ensure host-level governor is in performance mode.

Exceptions and compatibility notes:
- Some older model variants with large attention memory footprints may not support int8 kernels; throughput-mode will fall back to fp16 and mark kernel_fallback_reason in traces.
- Private deployments with constrained NICs should tune batch_timeout_ms higher to reduce packet amplification. Document any deviation via a change request ticket and specify compensating SLO targets.

Ownership and review cadence:
- Owner: Serving Runtime Performance Guild (team: engineering). Primary owner: Ava Brooks.
- Quarterly review: re-run the standard test matrix against the latest models and runtime builds.
- Emergency patch reviews: within 24 hours and documented in the release ticket.
